**Storing magnets:** keep bar magnets in pairs with unlike poles together and place soft iron **keepers** across the ends.
Generating electricity with a dynamo

A **dynamo** changes movement into electricity. When a coil of wire is turned inside a magnetic field (or a magnet is turned near a coil), electricity is produced. This is used on bicycles to light the lamp and, in a much bigger form, in power stations.
The electric bell

The bell uses an **electromagnet**. When the switch is pressed, current flows and the electromagnet attracts the soft iron armature, so the hammer strikes the gong. As the armature moves, it breaks the circuit, the electromagnet loses its magnetism and the spring pulls the armature back — closing the circuit again. This happens over and over, so the bell rings continuously.
Uses of magnets

Compasses for direction · loudspeakers, radios and telephones · electric bells · dynamos and generators · electric motors · cranes for lifting scrap metal · separating iron from other materials · fridge and cupboard door catches · magnetic cards and computer parts · picking up dropped pins.
Electricity and magnetism in the modern world of work

They run factories and machines, welding and metal work, transport (electric trains and cars), communication (phones, radio, internet), medical equipment in hospitals, and they create many jobs — electricians, engineers, technicians, phone repairers and solar installers.

**Mechanical advantage (M.A.) = Load ÷ Effort**
*Example:* A load of 600 N is lifted using an effort of 150 N. M.A. = 600 ÷ 150 = **4** (the machine multiplies the force 4 times)
*A machine has a mechanical advantage of 5 and lifts a load of 450 N. What effort is used?* Effort = 450 ÷ 5 = **90 N**
Definition
**Moment of a force:** The turning effect of a force, found by multiplying the force by its distance from the fulcrum.
The principle
**Load × distance of load from the fulcrum = Effort × distance of effort from the fulcrum**
When these are equal, the lever **balances**.
Worked examples

items: *A load of 40 N is placed 2 m from the fulcrum. An effort acts 4 m from the fulcrum on the other side. Find the effort needed.* 40 × 2 = E × 4 → 80 = 4E → E = **20 N**

blocks.x: **Lesson:** the further the effort is from the fulcrum, the **less** effort is needed.

blocks.x: How light travels
Light travels in **straight lines** — this is called **rectilinear propagation** — and it travels very fast (about 300,000 km per second). Light can travel through a vacuum, unlike sound.
**Simple proof:** line up three cards with holes in the same position; you can see a candle through them only when the holes are in a straight line.

The pin-hole camera

A closed box, blackened inside, with a tiny hole at the front and a screen of translucent paper at the back. Light from the object travels in straight lines through the hole and forms an image on the screen.

sections.title: 5. MANAGING A SCHOOL OR HOME WOOD PROJECT

**Prepare a nursery bed** — fine soil, shade and regular watering; sow the seeds.
